system_type_reason: Context database infrastructure that other agents build on; ships an optional bundled agent (Vikingbot).

repo_overview.summary: Context database for AI agents that manages memories, resources and skills through a filesystem paradigm (viking:// URIs) with three content tiers (L0 abstract, L1 overview, L2 full content), hierarchical retrieval and automatic long-term memory extraction from sessions. Contains two agentic loops: the ExtractLoop, a ReAct orchestrator in which an LLM reads the memory filesystem via tools and emits memory operations, and Vikingbot, a Nanobot-derived chat agent with shell/file/web/MCP/OpenViking tools and background subagents.

topology.justification: Vikingbot's main AgentLoop exposes a spawn tool (spawn.py:51-59) that starts a SubagentManager background task. Each subagent runs its own LLM loop with a dedicated system prompt, its own ToolRegistry, tool feedback and a stop condition (subagent.py:115-180, max 15 iterations). The result is published back as an InboundMessage (subagent.py:214-221) and the main agent processes it in a further _run_agent_loop (loop.py:1429-1442). A boss agent delegating to helper agents with their own loops counts as multi-agent. The ExtractLoop in openviking/session/memory/ is a separate single-agent ReAct loop.

resilience.name: iteration cap with forced final answer
resilience.what_it_is: The memory ExtractLoop runs at most max_iterations ReAct rounds (default 3). On the last round a user message orders the model to stop calling tools and return the final JSON, including an empty-shape skeleton of all expected fields for the no-change case. If no operations result, a RuntimeError is raised.
resilience.function_in_system: Bounds the memory extraction ReAct loop in ExtractLoop.run(). Caps LLM cost and latency per extraction and steers the model toward a usable final answer at the budget limit. Otherwise the model could keep exploring the memory filesystem via tools and the extraction would end with no operations.

resilience.name: five-layer tolerant JSON parsing of LLM output
resilience.what_it_is: parse_json_with_stability parses the model's final operations in five layers: (1) cut non-JSON text before and after the JSON, (2) json_repair, (3) structure tolerance (first element of a list, bare [] as no operations, unexpected fields dropped), (4) per-field type coercion (str/int/float/list), (5) Pydantic validation with strict=False where fields that still fail are dropped individually.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits between the LLM response and the operations model in ExtractLoop._call_llm (extract_loop.py:673-677). Absorbs malformed or slightly off-schema model output locally, which saves a retry round. Otherwise minor formatting slips such as markdown fences, trailing prose or wrong value types would fail the whole extraction.

resilience.name: per-operation error isolation on memory apply
resilience.what_it_is: MemoryUpdater.apply_operations wraps every upsert and every delete in its own try/except and collects failures in a MemoryUpdateResult. In addition, a delete whose URI was upserted in the same batch is skipped, since the LLM expresses a replace as delete plus create of the same name.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits after the ExtractLoop, where the model's operations are written to VikingFS. Contains a failing operation to its own URI so the rest of the batch still lands, and neutralizes a known LLM output pattern. Otherwise one bad operation would abort the whole memory update, and a replace would delete the just-written file.

resilience.name: iteration cap with tool-free final answer (Vikingbot)
resilience.what_it_is: The main AgentLoop runs at most max_iterations (default 50) LLM/tool rounds. When the cap is hit and the model has produced no final answer, a user message announces the limit and one extra LLM call with tools=[] forces a direct answer from the gathered results; if that stays empty, a fixed fallback text is returned. Subagents use a hard cap of 15 iterations with a fixed fallback result.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits around the whole tool-calling loop in _run_agent_loop and SubagentManager._run_subagent. Bounds runaway tool-calling and its cost per user message, and still converts the partial work into an answer. Otherwise a model that keeps calling tools loops indefinitely or ends with an empty reply.

resilience.name: tool-call error containment as observation
resilience.what_it_is: ToolRegistry.execute maps an unknown tool name to an 'Error: Tool ... not found' string and catches every exception raised by a tool, returning 'Error executing <name>: ...' as the tool result. The individual tools (shell, filesystem) follow the same pattern and return error strings.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits at the single tool dispatch point used by the main loop and subagents. Tool failures become tool messages that the LLM reads in the next iteration and can react to. Otherwise one failing or hallucinated tool call aborts the whole message processing.

resilience.name: JSON-schema validation of tool arguments
resilience.what_it_is: Before execution, Tool.validate_params recursively checks the LLM-supplied arguments against the tool's JSON schema (types, enum, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, required keys, array items). On any error the tool is skipped and an 'Error: Invalid parameters for tool ...' message listing all violations is returned. Tool arguments that fail JSON parsing are wrapped as {'raw': ...}, so the required-key check rejects them with the same error feedback.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in ToolRegistry.execute between the LLM's tool call and the tool implementation. Catches malformed arguments deterministically and feeds precise violations back to the model for correction. Otherwise malformed arguments reach the tool code and fail with opaque exceptions or act on wrong values.

resilience.name: MCP tool-call timeout and cancellation isolation
resilience.what_it_is: Every MCP tool call is wrapped in asyncio.wait_for with tool_timeout (default 30 s). Timeouts, SDK-internal cancellations and other exceptions are converted into result strings; a CancelledError is re-raised only when the agent task itself is being cancelled.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in MCPToolWrapper.execute, the adapter between the agent loop and external MCP servers. Keeps a hanging or crashing external server from blocking or cancelling the agent's turn and reports the failure to the model. Otherwise a stuck MCP server stalls the whole agent loop.

resilience.name: budgeted memory recall injection
resilience.what_it_is: Recalled user memories are filtered by score (>= 0.1), deduplicated by content hash and packed into the prompt under a total character budget (memory_recall_max_chars, default 4000) plus per-type budgets for events and entities. Memories beyond the budget are reduced to a summary or a URI-only entry, and the prompt tells the model to fetch those URIs with openviking_multi_read when needed.

Caps the context cost of automatic memory recall while keeping pointers to the rest. Otherwise every turn injects all retrieved memories in full and inflates the prompt.

resilience.name: session-window trimming with LLM memory consolidation
resilience.what_it_is: When a session exceeds memory_window (default 50) messages, the session is cloned, the live session is cut to the last min(10, max(2, memory_window // 2)) messages, and an LLM call condenses the older messages into a HISTORY.md entry and an updated long-term MEMORY.md. Session.get_history additionally caps prompt history at 50 messages.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in _process_message before the agent loop runs. Keeps the conversation history in the prompt bounded while preserving older content as summarized memory. Otherwise long chats overflow the context window or lose older facts silently.

resilience.name: token-budgeted OpenViking session context with local fallback
resilience.what_it_is: With session_context_enabled, the prompt history is rebuilt from OpenViking's archive overview plus recent messages under session_context_token_budget (default 3000), followed by the unsynced local tail. Before a turn, the session is committed to OpenViking when pending tokens reach commit_token_threshold or the message count reaches memory_window, keeping the most recent commit_keep_recent_count messages. If loading the OpenViking context fails, the loop falls back to the local session history. A failed sync marks last_sync_status as error, and the local session is then kept intact.
resilience.function_in_system: Sits in _process_message and _build_prompt_history as the alternative context-management path. Bounds prompt size by tokens and moves older turns into server-side memory, and the fallback keeps the agent answering when the OpenViking server is unreachable. Otherwise the history grows unbounded or a server outage breaks every turn.

resilience.name: classified transient-error retry with jittered exponential backoff
resilience.what_it_is: Every VLM call in the openai and litellm backends runs through retry_sync/retry_async. classify_api_error matches the error text against pattern lists and labels it transient, quota_exceeded, auth, permanent, input_too_large or content_safety. resilience.name: ordered multi-credential failover with timed failback
resilience.what_it_is: When the vlm config lists more than one credential, get_vlm_instance wraps one backend per credential in MultiCredentialVLM; the legacy primary/backup config builds FailoverVLM. Each request starts at the active credential and cycles through the ring once. Request-level errors (400, input_too_large, content_safety) re-raise immediately. Auth, quota and retry-exhausted transient errors advance to the next credential, and the credential that succeeds becomes active. OrderedCredentialSwitcher moves back one priority step after 600 s or 50 requests on the fallback. If every credential fails, AllCredentialsFailedError carries the aggregated errors. Keeps extraction running when one API key hits its quota, gets revoked or its provider has a longer outage, and returns to the preferred credential once it recovers. Fail-fast on request-level errors avoids burning every credential on a request that fails everywhere. Otherwise a quota exhaustion on the single key stops all memory extraction until an operator intervenes.

resilience.name: oversized tool-output externalization with synopsis stubs and read-back refs
resilience.what_it_is: When a message is added to an OpenViking session, every tool output above threshold_chars=20000 is moved to a ToolResultStore file in VikingFS under a sha256-based ref. Otherwise a single large command or file dump fills the agent's context budget on every later turn.

resilience.name: schema-scoped memory locks held across the extraction loop
resilience.what_it_is: Before a memory extraction run, SessionCompressorV2 derives exact file lock paths and subtree lock paths from the memory schemas and the user scope, then acquires them as one batch in a retry loop (v2_lock_retry_interval_seconds=0.2, v2_lock_max_retries=0 meaning unlimited, TimeoutError once a positive limit is hit, rate-limited warning logs). The locks stay held through the whole ExtractLoop run and the apply of its operations and are released in a finally block. Each extraction phase in _run_extract_phase uses the same scheme. Lock files carry a timestamp and count as stale after lock_expire (default 300 s): an acquirer that meets a stale exact or tree lock deletes it and logs a warning, and a LockManager background task started with the service checks every 60 s and releases in-process handles that stopped refreshing for longer than lock_expire.
resilience.function_in_system: Wraps the memory ExtractLoop in session commit. Serializes concurrent extractions (parallel commits of sessions for the same user or agent) that read and patch the same memory files, so the read-before-write view the loop builds stays valid until its patches land. Otherwise two concurrent runs read the same memory, both apply their edits and one silently overwrites the other. Stale-lock reclamation frees memory paths left locked by a crashed or leaked extraction, so later commits for the same user can proceed. Otherwise one crash blocks all future memory extraction for that scope. The extraction handle has no refresh task, so a run longer than lock_expire can lose its locks to a concurrent extraction.

resilience.function_in_system: Wraps the memory ExtractLoop in the asynchronous commit path. Serializes extraction runs per session so each run builds on the completed overview of the previous archive, and contains a failed run to its own archive. Otherwise out-of-order commits extract memories against a stale overview, and one failed archive stalls every later commit of the session. A hard crash leaves neither marker, so the wait for that archive has no upper bound.
